## Overview

You have **one daily sea surface temperature field** on a regular lat–lon grid. You want **|∇SST|** — how sharply SST changes **across space** on that day — in **°C km⁻¹**. That is a standard way to represent **thermal fronts** when linking oceanography to tracks.

This page builds a **50 × 50** toy ocean: **stable SST** on both sides of the map, with a **steep meridional front** through the centre (like a front crossing an otherwise uniform water mass). Then we compute |∇SST| with the same centred-difference recipe used on many reanalysis grids.

**You need:** R and [`terra`](https://rspatial.org/terra/).

**This is not:** day-to-day SST change at one point; a front-probability layer; or a gradient of regional mean SST.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Load terra




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pacman::p_load(terra)
```
:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2. Fine grid + open-ocean front through the middle

**50 × 50** cells on **0.5° × 0.5°** (~**0.01°** per cell). SST is **~21 °C** away from the front; a **narrow east–west transition** (~2 °C step) sits on the **central meridian** — steep enough that |∇SST| peaks on a thin band.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
n <- 50L
col_c <- (n + 1) / 2 # front line runs north–south through the map centre

sst <- terra::rast(
  ncols = n,
  nrows = n,
  xmin = 170,
  xmax = 170.5,
  ymin = -45,
  ymax = -44.5,
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
)

# plogis((col - col_c) * k): large k → front only a few cells wide.
# Subtract 1.5 so west/east plateaus sit near 21 °C with a ~3 °C step across the front.
k_steep <- 3.5
sst_mat <- outer(1:n, 1:n, function(row, col) {
  open_ocean <- 21 + 0.002 * (row - col_c) # tiny variation — mostly stable water
  front_step <- 3 * plogis((col - col_c) * k_steep) - 1.5
  open_ocean + front_step
})

terra::values(sst) <- matrix(sst_mat, nrow = n, ncol = n, byrow = TRUE)

c(
  res_lon_deg = terra::res(sst)[1],
  res_lat_deg = terra::res(sst)[2],
  sst_min = min(sst_mat, na.rm = TRUE),
  sst_max = max(sst_mat, na.rm = TRUE)
)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
res_lon_deg res_lat_deg     sst_min     sst_max 
      0.010       0.010      19.451      22.549 
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot(sst, main = "Toy SST (°C) — stable ocean, front through centre")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/plot-sst-1.png){width=960}
:::
:::


West and east of the middle column should look **almost uniform**; the colour change is **concentrated** on the centre line.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3. Cell width in kilometres


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
res <- terra::res(sst)
clat <- mean(
  terra::yFromCell(sst, seq_len(min(5000L, terra::ncell(sst)))),
  na.rm = TRUE
)
dx_km <- as.numeric(res[1]) * 111.32 * cos(clat * pi / 180)
dy_km <- as.numeric(res[2]) * 111.32
c(dx_km = dx_km, dy_km = dy_km, mean_lat = clat)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
      dx_km       dy_km    mean_lat 
  0.7905784   1.1132000 -44.7500000 
```


:::
:::


On real NetCDF, `summary(SST)` should look like ocean **°C** (~0–35), not Kelvin (~273+).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4. Centred differences → |∇SST|


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
sst_grad_magnitude_layer <- function(sst) {
  if (is.null(sst) || !terra::ncell(sst)) return(NULL)
  res <- terra::res(sst)
  clat <- mean(
    terra::yFromCell(sst, seq_len(min(5000L, terra::ncell(sst)))),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
  dx_km <- as.numeric(res[1]) * 111.32 * cos(clat * pi / 180)
  dy_km <- as.numeric(res[2]) * 111.32
  if (!is.finite(dx_km) || dx_km <= 0 || !is.finite(dy_km) || dy_km <= 0) return(NULL)
  w_x <- matrix(c(0, 0, 0, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 0, 0, 0), nrow = 3, ncol = 3)
  w_y <- matrix(c(0, -0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.5, 0), nrow = 3, ncol = 3)
  gx <- terra::focal(sst, w = w_x, fun = sum, na.rm = TRUE, pad = TRUE) / dx_km
  gy <- terra::focal(sst, w = w_y, fun = sum, na.rm = TRUE, pad = TRUE) / dy_km
  sqrt(gx^2 + gy^2)
}

grad <- sst_grad_magnitude_layer(sst)
summary(grad, na.rm = TRUE)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
   focal_sum        
 Min.   : 0.001797  
 1st Qu.: 0.001797  
 Median : 0.001797  
 Mean   : 0.972796  
 3rd Qu.: 0.001797  
 Max.   :17.491047  
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(sst, main = "SST (°C)")
plot(grad, main = expression("|"*nabla*SST|" (°C km"^-1*")"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/plot-both-1.png){width=960}
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
:::


**|∇SST|** should **peak on the central front** and stay **low** on the stable flanks (small north–south background trend adds weak structure off the front).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. Quick checks


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
flat <- sst * 0 + 21
g_flat <- sst_grad_magnitude_layer(flat)
g_front <- sst_grad_magnitude_layer(sst)
mean_flat <- terra::global(g_flat, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
mean_front <- terra::global(g_front, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
max_front <- terra::global(g_front, "max", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
stopifnot(is.finite(mean_flat), is.finite(mean_front))
stopifnot(mean_front > mean_flat, max_front > 0.05)
c(flat_mean = mean_flat, front_mean = mean_front, front_max = max_front)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
 flat_mean front_mean  front_max 
 0.8982694  0.9727964 17.4910473 
```


:::
:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 6. Common mix-ups

| Idea | Reality |
|------|---------|
| Gradient = day-to-day SST at a point | **Spatial** differences on **one** daily layer |
| Kelvin vs Celsius | Differences match; report SST in one convention |
| Coastal high \|∇SST\| | Often bathymetry/coast, not open-ocean fronts |
| Fine grid = all filaments resolved | ~0.08° only partly resolves mesoscale fronts |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 7. Real data

1. One daily SST layer on a grid you trust.  
2. Same function per day if needed.  
3. `terra::extract` at track lon/lat (check −180…180 vs 0…360).  
4. Aggregate to your model time step.

See [Copernicus Marine](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/) for GLORYS-style products.
